messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Aurora: performance SLO & streaming follow-up

Thanks again for the time earlier today — great discussion. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align on an implementation plan.

What we heard (confirm / correct):
- TTFT targets: Aurora is aiming for TTFT in the single-token streaming case to be in the sub-200ms neighborhood at the 95th percentile for desktop users, with tighter goals for critical flows.
- Traffic profile: baseline 200 QPS, autoscale up to ~800 QPS peak during morning batch windows; concurrency expected up to ~120 simultaneous end-users.
- Response sizes: median ~200 tokens, tail up to 1k tokens for long-form generation.
- Streaming requirements: desktop prefers SSE (server-sent events) for simplicity; mobile team is leaning toward WebSocket due to connection stability and two-way control.
- Chunk cadence preferences: want small chunks early (to hit TTFT goals) — roughly 40-80 tokens per chunk, but cadence frequency needs to account for bursty inputs and mobile jitter.
- Reliability: fallback to non-streaming (full payload) acceptable if network conditions cause chunk delivery > 500ms or the runtime falls back due to load.

Redwood proposal (high level):
- Pilot stage: Hosted API pilot with a canary region for Aurora traffic (we'll route a small % initially). We can instrument TTFT at both ingress and after kernel execution to measure true server-side TTFT.
- Cadence approach: default cadence = whichever comes first: 200ms or 64 tokens. We recommend starting conservative (200ms/64 tokens) and tightening after pilot telemetry.
- Backpressure and fallbacks: automatic dynamic cadence (we lower chunk frequency under high load), plus explicit fallback to non-streaming if chunk gap > 500ms or if KV cache miss rates cause >10% extra token cost.
- Measurements: we'll report TTFT p50/p95/p99, token throughput, concurrency breakdown, and end-to-end client-observed first byte latency.

Action items / next steps:
1) I attach an initial SLO proposal and the load profile CSV we used during the call. Please confirm the baseline/peak numbers and the target TTFT percentiles.
2) Rajiv / Elena: can you confirm whether mobile must use WebSocket for the pilot or if SSE is acceptable for mobile MVP?
3) Redwood: we will prepare a short pilot runbook and an updated SLO PDF that includes explicit measurement definitions and rollback criteria.
4) Schedule a 30-min technical sync next week to align on instrumentation and sampling.

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Do you need a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for deterministic TTFT, or is hosted with burst guarantees acceptable for the pilot?
- Legal/procurement timeline for SLOs and SLA attachments. (I copied contracts@aurorahealth.com in case procurement wants to weigh in.)

Thanks — I’ll draft the runbook and send it to you by EOD Monday.

Best,
Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) TTFT percentiles: the mobile product team actually needs a two-tiered requirement: TTFT p95 < 200ms (interactive flows) and p99 < 400ms for desktop critical paths. The p99 numbers are important for our SLA with clinical partners.
2) Throughput/scale: the 800 QPS peak is accurate for peak windows, but note that for some internal workflows we expect short-lived spikes to 1.2k QPS for <5 minutes — we need to understand burst handling.
3) WebSocket vs SSE: desktop can do SSE; mobile prefers WebSocket because of flaky mobile carriers and ability to replay missed chunks. Can you outline how Redwood's runtime supports both and where behavior differs?
4) Security/VPC: procurement asked whether Redwood supports a VPC/private deployment for Aurora (we’re evaluating hosted first but procurement wants options). I attached a procurement timeline.

We'll review the SLO PDF and the load CSV today and route to legal.

—Rajiv
Director, Platform Engineering | Aurora Health

Appreciate the clarifications — good call-outs. Short answers and a proposed staged plan below.

TTFT percentiles
- We will instrument and report p50/p95/p99 from the server-side and also provide a client-observed metric package for your QA team. For contractual SLAs, we can map to server-side p95/p99; client-observed metrics are often noisier but we’ll include both.

Burst handling
- Hosted runtime supports short bursts to ~1.5x baseline with autoscaling; for deterministic handling of 1.2k short spikes we recommend either: (a) Reserved/Dedicated pool sized to handle expected peak, or (b) Hosted + configured burst capacity and a short buffering layer at the ingress (we can provide recommended buffer settings). For pilot we suggest option (b) and validate burst behavior.

SSE vs WebSocket behavior (high level)
- SSE: one-way stream, simple reconnect semantics; good for desktop/browser clients.
- WebSocket: two-way, allows client ACKs and explicit retransmit requests which helps with mobile carrier variability.
- Redwood runtime supports both; chunking/cadence controls are applied server-side consistently. For mobile we recommend WebSocket + small client ACK window to allow limited retransmit, but we can demo both approaches during the sync.

Proposed cadence & fallback (pilot)
- Initial cadence: 200ms or 64 tokens (start conservative).
- If KV cache hit and response generation is fast, we tighten to 120ms / 48 tokens after 48 hours of stable telemetry.
- Fallback: switch to whole-response (non-stream) if chunk gap > 500ms for more than 3 consecutive chunks or if chunk error rate > 5%.

Pilot plan & timeline
- Week 0: confirm sampling and instrumentation tags (we’ll give a short JSON schema for span names).
- Week 1: start Hosted pilot in us-west region at 5% traffic. Capture TTFT & client-observed metrics.
- Week 2: scale to 25% traffic if metrics look healthy; validate burst window handling.

Next steps
- I’ll send a one-page runbook and an updated SLO PDF (explicit measurement definitions + rollback criteria) by EOD Monday.
- Can we lock a 30-min technical sync on Tue 11/30 at 10:00 AM PT? If that works, I’ll invite the Redwood infra lead and our runtime engineer.
